newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Sept coffee exports seen at 1.4 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Sept coffee exports seen at 1.4 mln bags.

text.p: Brazilian coffee exports in September are estimated at 1.4 million bags, down from 1.566 million bags in August, according to the head of the primary commodities department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry.

Mauricio Assis, who met with the Brazilian Coffee Committee (CBC) ahead of the upcoming meeting of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) in London at the end of the month, said Brazil's policy for the ACPC conference was unchanged. He said Brazil's export quota for the 1996/97 harvest remained at 15 million bags.

Brazil's 1996/97 harvest, which is estimated at 24-25 million bags, will not be sufficient to cover exports and domestic consumption of 11 million bags, Assis said. Brazil also expects to export 2.5 million bags of soluble coffee.
"We will have to use private and government stocks," Assis said.
He said the creation of a coffee council, which would include private and public sector representatives and would determine future Brazilian coffee policy, was in the final stages of being resolved.
"Ministers are still studying the issue, but I believe it will be resolved quickly," Assis said.
He said the exemption of primary and semi-manufactured exports from the so-called ICMS tax on the circulation of goods and services would be positive for the coffee industry.
"Brazil will become more competitive. Producers will increase their incomes," Assis said.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
